title: Snack Packaging
summary: A rebrand for Insane Grain, a sorghum-based health snack whose packaging was far quieter than its name. The new pouch is built to grab younger, trend-conscious snackers without losing the health story.

hero.alt: Insane Grain pouch: a halftone mouth, red chili and flame linework in red, black and white, with tall condensed type.

overview.challenge: The old packaging didn’t carry the energy or boldness the name promised, and it wasn’t speaking to the younger, trend-conscious audience the brand wanted.
overview.solution: A loud collage system: a halftone mouth, real chilies and inky flame linework, locked into hard red, black and white blocks with tall condensed type.
overview.outcome: A pouch that sells heat first. The health claims (sorghum, gut health, 47% less fat) get their own black band, so they still read at a glance.

blocks.label: 01 — Research
blocks.heading: Borrowing from collage posters
blocks.body: I pulled collage portraits, halftone photography and loud poster typography: work that feels cut up, layered and a little unhinged, which is exactly what the name asks for.
blocks.alt: Moodboard of collage portraits, halftone photography and bold poster typography.
blocks.caption: Moodboard: collage, halftone and poster type references.

blocks.label: 02 — Sketches
blocks.heading: Two early directions
blocks.body: A digital collage tested how photography, halftone and flat colour could share one surface. A marker sketch blocked out the grid underneath it.
blocks.alt: Two early pouch studies on black: a digital collage and a marker sketch.
blocks.caption: Collage study (left) and marker sketch (right).
